title: Work Claimed or Offset Advanced Before Processing, With No Lease or Redelivery
pattern: A hand-written consumer marks a job claimed/processed, or commits a stream offset, in the same call that hands the work to the worker, before processing has completed, with no lease expiry, visibility timeout or redelivery if the worker dies.
why_bad: If the worker crashes, hangs or fails after the claim or offset commit, the job stays claimed forever or the message is skipped: delivery is silently at-most-once. Nothing distinguishes "in progress" from "abandoned", so lost work is only discovered by reconciliation.
detection: Queue or stream consumer code that persists a `claimed`/`processed`/`done` flag or a consumer offset before or at the moment it returns the work item, with no claim timestamp/lease that expires, no later ack/commit after processing, and no sweeper that re-queues stale claims.
counterexample: Leased claims (`claimed_until`, visibility timeouts, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` inside a transaction that also records completion); offsets committed after processing; work whose loss is explicitly acceptable (best-effort telemetry). Broker auto-acknowledge settings are a separate criterion.
fix:
Claim with a lease and complete explicitly after processing; commit offsets only after the message is handled.
```rust
let task = store.claim_next(worker_id, Duration::from_secs(60))?; // claimed_until = now + 60s
process(&task)?;
store.complete(task.id, worker_id)?; // expired leases are re-queued by a sweeper
```
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals* (2019), Ch. 8; Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* (2017), Ch. 11 "Stream Processing".
